transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I came because people keep telling me this foreclosure is just, you know, paperwork and missed payments, like I don’t understand bills or dates or whatever. But that’s not what’s happening. The bank and the loan servicer have been working together, and I’m pretty sure people at my job have been involved too—quietly, behind my back—to push me out of my house.

And it’s been going on for almost two years. I mean, they can show me all the papers they want, but papers can be made to say anything. I see the way people act, the timing of things, the little comments. Even at work, people who normally barely talk to me suddenly know things they shouldn’t. So… that’s why I’m here, I guess. Everyone acts like I’m supposed to just accept their version of it.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?

I don’t know… I mean, I get tired like anyone else. Sometimes I don’t sleep great when things are stressful, but “unusually energized” sounds kind of like one of those check-box phrases. I still have to get up for work, open the store, deal with everyone’s schedules, and then people act like if I’m alert it means something.

So… no, not that I’ve really noticed. I wouldn’t say I’m running around with extra energy or not needing sleep. It’s more just, you know, there’s a lot going on.
Have you ever heard voices when no one else was there?

Voices? I mean… not like in the way people make it sound on TV, no. I don’t sit there hearing someone talking in an empty room or anything.

Sometimes I hear people talking nearby and I wonder if they’re talking about me, but that’s just because of the situation and how people have been acting. Like at work, when people lower their voices as I come around—anyone would notice that. But hearing voices when nobody is there? I don’t think so.
Have you found yourself feeling much less interested in being around other people than you used to?

I don’t know if I’d say “less interested.” I mean, I’m around people all day at work, so it’s not like I’m living in a cave or something. Though honestly, after dealing with customers and staff and all the little side conversations, I sometimes just want to go home and have quiet.

But that’s normal, right? My sister does that too—she works at a salon and she says by the end of the day she doesn’t want anyone talking to her, not even the TV on loud. So I don’t know. I guess I haven’t really been keeping track of whether I want to be around people more or less.
Have you had any major medical illness or brain injury around the time these concerns began?

I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had the usual stuff—colds, headaches, you know, the kind of thing where you still go to work because nobody else can cover the shift. But nothing major that I can think of.

Brain injury… no, not that I know of. I’ve bumped my head before, like everyone has, but not some big accident or hospital thing. It’s funny, because at work we had this whole safety training about ladders and falling boxes, and half the people weren’t even listening, which is exactly how accidents happen, but… no, I don’t think there was anything like that around when all this started.
Have you had a period when you felt deeply depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I don’t know… “deeply depressed” sounds like a very specific thing. I’ve had bad days, sure. Everybody does. Especially in retail—people think supervisors just stand around, but you’re the one who gets yelled at when the schedule doesn’t work or when someone calls out.

But most of the day, nearly every day… I’m not sure I’d put it that way. Sometimes I’m worn out or frustrated, and then I’ll go home and just not want to deal with anything, but that could just be being tired. I guess I haven’t really been measuring it like that.
Have you believed that anyone was controlling your thoughts?

Controlling my thoughts? No, not like putting thoughts in my head or anything like that.

What I’ve been trying to explain is more… people keep acting like this foreclosure is just paperwork, like I missed some payments and that’s the whole story. But I know it’s not just that. The bank, the loan servicer, and even some people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. And every time they show me another paper, it’s like they expect me to ignore what I’ve been seeing for almost two years.
Have other people told you that your speech or thoughts are hard to follow or seem jumbled?

I don’t think people have said it like that, no. I mean, sometimes at work people act like they don’t understand what I’m getting at, but that’s usually because they’re only hearing half of what I’m saying or they’re busy looking at the schedule or their phone.

“Jumbled” sounds… I don’t know, like I’m not making sense at all. I don’t think that’s what’s happening. Sometimes I have to explain the background first, because if you don’t know all the pieces, then of course it sounds confusing. Like with paperwork—people want the short version, but the short version leaves out the important part. So… I’m not sure. No one’s really told me that directly.
Has anything impossible happened to you, like someone using special powers or technology to influence you or your surroundings?

Special powers? No, I’m not saying wizards or mind control or anything like that.

It’s more real-world than that. Paperwork, phone calls, people “misplacing” things, changing what they told me before. Everyone keeps acting like the foreclosure is just missed payments and forms, like I’m supposed to accept whatever the bank or the loan servicer says. But I know they’ve been working together—quietly—with even some people at my job, trying to push me out of my house.

And I know that sounds like a lot, but this has been almost two years of little things lining up. No amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing.
Have you ever felt that ordinary things—like TV shows, radio, or strangers’ conversations—were sending you special messages meant specifically for you?

TV shows and radio? No, not really like they’re sending me coded messages or anything. I don’t sit there thinking the news anchor is talking directly to me.

It’s more that ordinary things people brush off—like a comment at work, or a letter arriving right after I ask a question, or someone suddenly changing what they said before—those things aren’t random. That’s what people keep not understanding. They want to make it sound like this foreclosure is just paperwork and missed payments, but I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house.

And I’ve been seeing it for almost two years, so when people show me another form like that settles it, it doesn’t. It just feels like they’re trying to make me ignore what’s right in front of me.
Aside from what you believe is happening with your house and the people involved, have you had any other unusual beliefs that others found hard to accept?

Not really other things, no. I mean, people keep trying to make it sound like I have all these “unusual beliefs,” but it’s really this one situation.

I’m here because everyone keeps acting like the foreclosure is just paperwork and missed payments, like if they wave enough forms at me I’m supposed to stop asking questions. But I know the bank and the loan servicer have been working together, and honestly even some people at my job, quietly, to push me out of my house.

And it’s not like I woke up one day and decided that. It’s been almost two years of things happening, little things that line up. People changing what they said, things going missing, timing that’s too exact. So no, I don’t have some other belief about… I don’t know, aliens or the TV or whatever. It’s this. No amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing.
Have you ever felt that someone was spying on you or following you?

Spying or following… I mean, not like some person in a trench coat behind me, no. But I do feel watched in the sense that things get back to people too fast, you know?

Like at work, I’ll say something about the house or question one thing, and then suddenly there’s another call, another letter, someone “clarifying” something they already told me. And everyone says, oh, that’s just how foreclosure paperwork goes, missed payments, forms, deadlines. But that’s what I’m trying to explain — it isn’t just paperwork. The bank, the loan servicer, even people at my job, they’re quietly working together to push me out of my house.

And I’ve been seeing it for almost two years. So maybe not followed down the street, exactly, but yes, I feel like they’re keeping tabs on me. Papers don’t erase that.
Have you ever felt that other people could hear your thoughts?

Other people hearing my thoughts? No… I don’t think so. I mean, how would I even know that, right?

Sometimes people answer before I’ve fully explained something, but that’s usually because they’re assuming they know what I mean, or they’ve already decided what side they’re on. Like at work, people do that all the time—cut you off, finish your sentence, act like you’re being difficult when you’re just trying to be clear.

But no, I’m not saying anyone can hear my thoughts inside my head. That’s not really what I mean.
Since these concerns began, have you had trouble keeping up with your work or taking care of yourself the way you used to?

I mean… mostly I still do what I’m supposed to do. I get up, I go to work, I supervise my team, I do the schedules, deal with customers when they’re upset — which is funny because people act like I can’t handle anything, but I’m the one they call when somebody is yelling at the register.

And I take care of myself, yes. I’m not just lying around or anything like that.

It gets harder when something comes in the mail, or the bank calls, or there’s paperwork at work that seems connected to all this. Then I can get pulled into it, because I have to look at it carefully. I can’t just ignore it like everyone wants me to. So that’s when things get disrupted, not just every day for no reason.
Have people told you that your face or voice seem less expressive than they used to?

Less expressive? I don’t know… nobody has said it to me like that. I mean, people tell women to “smile” or say you sound short when you’re just being direct, especially at work. I deal with customers all day, so I have to keep my voice kind of controlled or everything turns into a whole scene.

But if you mean like my face not moving or my voice being flat, I haven’t really noticed that. Nobody’s pulled me aside and said that, no.
Outside of the situation with your house, have you had any other experiences that made you feel people were plotting against you?

Outside of the house… well, it doesn’t really stay outside the house, that’s the thing. People try to make it sound like it’s just foreclosure paperwork, late payments, forms, whatever, but it’s not just that.

The bank and the loan servicer have been working this in a way that’s too coordinated to be accidental. And then at work, certain people started acting differently too — like they knew things they shouldn’t know, or they’d make little comments right after I’d gotten some letter or call. It’s all connected, even if everybody wants to act like I’m “reading into it.”

I’ve been watching it for almost two years now. Papers don’t change what I’ve seen. They can print anything on letterhead and call it normal procedure, but that doesn’t mean there isn’t a plan behind it. So yes, I guess I do think people have been quietly working together, not just with the house, but around me, to push me out.
Have these beliefs about the bank and people at work been present continuously for more than one month?

Yes… more than a month. Way more. It’s been, I guess, about a year and nine months now — since those foreclosure notices started coming and the bank calls were taking over everything at home.

I remember because at first I thought it was just one mistake, like somebody in an office clicking the wrong thing, but then it kept going. And once your home life gets wrapped around phone calls and letters, you start noticing who says what and when. So no, this hasn’t been a short thing. It’s been going on a long time.
While all this with the house has been going on, have there been times when you felt extremely high or euphoric?

Extremely high? No, I mean… I don’t think so. I’ve had moments where I felt kind of energized, like when I thought I had figured out what they were doing, but that’s not “euphoric,” that’s just… you know, relief for five minutes before the next thing drops.

Honestly, “high” makes it sound like I’m walking around happy and carefree, and that’s not really how this has been. It’s more like being alert. Like at work, when you’re watching three registers, a customer return, someone calling out sick, and then somebody from corporate wants numbers—your brain just stays on. But that’s not the same as being happy. So no, I wouldn’t call it extremely high or euphoric.
Have you had trouble getting yourself started to do everyday things, even when you wanted to?

I mean… not usually, no. If it’s just a normal day, I can get myself up and go to work. I supervise my team, I deal with the schedule, customer complaints, people needing overrides, all of that. Retail doesn’t really let you just sit around deciding whether to start or not, you know?

Where it gets hard is when something comes in the mail, or the bank calls, or there’s paperwork at work that feels like it’s connected to the house situation. Then I can get stuck on it. Like I’ll be trying to make breakfast or get dressed, and then I’m thinking about what that form really means, or why that call happened right before something at work. That’s when starting things gets messy.

But otherwise, I still take care of myself and do what I have to do. It’s mostly when those things show up and pull me back into it.
Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

I don’t think so… not like, seeing a person standing there that nobody else sees or anything like that.

Sometimes I notice things other people don’t seem to notice, like a car parked too long, or someone at work looking at me a certain way, or papers being moved from where I left them — but that’s different, right? That’s not like a movie where there’s something floating in the room. It’s more that other people don’t pay attention, or they act like they didn’t see it.

So… no, I don’t think I’ve seen things that weren’t there. At least not in that sense.

target_item.reason: The question is about thought broadcasting, specifically whether other people can hear my thoughts, and the provided symptom profile only covers fixed persecutory beliefs about the foreclosure, not this symptom.

patient.answer:
Other people hearing my thoughts? No… I don’t think so. I mean, how would I even know that, right?

Sometimes people answer before I’ve fully explained something, but that’s usually because they’re assuming they know what I mean, or they’ve already decided what side they’re on. Like at work, people do that all the time—cut you off, finish your sentence, act like you’re being difficult when you’re just trying to be clear.

But no, I’m not saying anyone can hear my thoughts inside my head. That’s not really what I mean.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been marked deterioration in work or self-care functioning, which helps distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum psychoses.
doctor.question: Since these concerns began, have you had trouble keeping up with your work or taking care of yourself the way you used to?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: When the foreclosure is not involved, I still get up for work, supervise my team, handle schedules and customer issues, and take care of myself. The problems mostly start when mail, bank calls, or workplace paperwork seem tied to what I believe is happening with the house.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether functioning at work and self-care have declined since the concerns began, which directly matches this profile item about overall functioning being mostly preserved except where affected by the delusion.

patient.answer:
I mean… mostly I still do what I’m supposed to do. I get up, I go to work, I supervise my team, I do the schedules, deal with customers when they’re upset — which is funny because people act like I can’t handle anything, but I’m the one they call when somebody is yelling at the register.

And I take care of myself, yes. I’m not just lying around or anything like that.

It gets harder when something comes in the mail, or the bank calls, or there’s paperwork at work that seems connected to all this. Then I can get pulled into it, because I have to look at it carefully. I can’t just ignore it like everyone wants me to. So that’s when things get disrupted, not just every day for no reason.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are persistent negative symptoms, especially reduced emotional expression, to help distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum illnesses.
doctor.question: Have people told you that your face or voice seem less expressive than they used to?

target_item.reason: The question asks about reduced facial or vocal expressiveness, which is not covered by any listed symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Less expressive? I don’t know… nobody has said it to me like that. I mean, people tell women to “smile” or say you sound short when you’re just being direct, especially at work. I deal with customers all day, so I have to keep my voice kind of controlled or everything turns into a whole scene.

But if you mean like my face not moving or my voice being flat, I haven’t really noticed that. Nobody’s pulled me aside and said that, no.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief has remained circumscribed or whether there are additional psychotic symptoms emerging, to help distinguish persistent delusional disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum conditions.
doctor.question: Outside of the situation with your house, have you had any other experiences that made you feel people were plotting against you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just paperwork and missed payments, but I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house, and no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about persecutory beliefs—whether there are other situations where I believe people are plotting against me—so it directly relates to the delusions profile.

patient.answer:
Outside of the house… well, it doesn’t really stay outside the house, that’s the thing. People try to make it sound like it’s just foreclosure paperwork, late payments, forms, whatever, but it’s not just that.

The bank and the loan servicer have been working this in a way that’s too coordinated to be accidental. And then at work, certain people started acting differently too — like they knew things they shouldn’t know, or they’d make little comments right after I’d gotten some letter or call. It’s all connected, even if everybody wants to act like I’m “reading into it.”

I’ve been watching it for almost two years now. Papers don’t change what I’ve seen. They can print anything on letterhead and call it normal procedure, but that doesn’t mean there isn’t a plan behind it. So yes, I guess I do think people have been quietly working together, not just with the house, but around me, to push me out.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional symptoms have persisted for at least one month continuously, to distinguish a persistent delusional disorder from acute/transient psychotic disorder and help separate from schizophrenia-spectrum conditions.
doctor.question: Have these beliefs about the bank and people at work been present continuously for more than one month?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about 1 year and 9 months, since the foreclosure notices and bank calls started taking over our home life.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the beliefs have been present, specifically whether they have continued for more than one month.

patient.answer:
Yes… more than a month. Way more. It’s been, I guess, about a year and nine months now — since those foreclosure notices started coming and the bank calls were taking over everything at home.

I remember because at first I thought it was just one mistake, like somebody in an office clicking the wrong thing, but then it kept going. And once your home life gets wrapped around phone calls and letters, you start noticing who says what and when. So no, this hasn’t been a short thing. It’s been going on a long time.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief is accompanied by prominent mood symptoms occurring at the same time, which would help distinguish delusional disorder from schizoaffective disorder or psychotic bipolar disorder.
doctor.question: While all this with the house has been going on, have there been times when you felt extremely high or euphoric?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about episodes of extremely high or euphoric mood, which relates to manic or hypomanic symptoms. The provided symptom profile does not include mania, hypomania, or elevated mood symptoms.

patient.answer:
Extremely high? No, I mean… I don’t think so. I’ve had moments where I felt kind of energized, like when I thought I had figured out what they were doing, but that’s not “euphoric,” that’s just… you know, relief for five minutes before the next thing drops.

Honestly, “high” makes it sound like I’m walking around happy and carefree, and that’s not really how this has been. It’s more like being alert. Like at work, when you’re watching three registers, a customer return, someone calling out sick, and then somebody from corporate wants numbers—your brain just stays on. But that’s not the same as being happy. So no, I wouldn’t call it extremely high or euphoric.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent negative symptoms, which would help distinguish schizophrenia from delusional disorder and other psychotic disorders.
doctor.question: Have you had trouble getting yourself started to do everyday things, even when you wanted to?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: When the foreclosure is not involved, I still get up for work, supervise my team, handle schedules and customer issues, and take care of myself. The problems mostly start when mail, bank calls, or workplace paperwork seem tied to what I believe is happening with the house.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about ability to initiate everyday activities and general functioning outside the delusional concern, which is best covered by this profile.

patient.answer:
I mean… not usually, no. If it’s just a normal day, I can get myself up and go to work. I supervise my team, I deal with the schedule, customer complaints, people needing overrides, all of that. Retail doesn’t really let you just sit around deciding whether to start or not, you know?

Where it gets hard is when something comes in the mail, or the bank calls, or there’s paperwork at work that feels like it’s connected to the house situation. Then I can get stuck on it. Like I’ll be trying to make breakfast or get dressed, and then I’m thinking about what that form really means, or why that call happened right before something at work. That’s when starting things gets messy.

But otherwise, I still take care of myself and do what I have to do. It’s mostly when those things show up and pull me back into it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms are limited to a single non-bizarre delusional theme with otherwise preserved functioning, which would favor delusional disorder over schizophrenia-spectrum or mood-related psychosis.
doctor.question: Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

target_item.reason: The question is about visual hallucinations—seeing things other people could not see—but the provided symptom profile only covers delusions, duration, and functioning, not hallucinations.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… not like, seeing a person standing there that nobody else sees or anything like that.

Sometimes I notice things other people don’t seem to notice, like a car parked too long, or someone at work looking at me a certain way, or papers being moved from where I left them — but that’s different, right? That’s not like a movie where there’s something floating in the room. It’s more that other people don’t pay attention, or they act like they didn’t see it.

So… no, I don’t think I’ve seen things that weren’t there. At least not in that sense.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main presenting concern
opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a single, persistent persecutory delusional system lasting about 1 year and 9 months, centered on the belief that the bank, loan servicer, and coworkers are coordinating to push her out of her house. There is no clear evidence of hallucinations, formal thought disorder, negative symptoms, manic syndrome, major depressive syndrome, or medical/neurological cause. Functioning is relatively preserved outside the delusion-focused disruptions, supporting persistent delusional disorder rather than schizophrenia, schizoaffective/bipolar psychosis, acute transient psychosis, or organic psychosis.
